title: A Powerful Nor’easter Is Taking Shape. How It Could Affect Your Forecast.
summary: The forecast for this weekend became a lot clearer on Wednesday, but meteorologists warned that the storm’s exact path was still uncertain.

A powerful storm that is expected to move up the East Coast this weekend was still organizing itself off the Carolinas on Wednesday afternoon. While the storm is expected to intensify between Thursday and Friday, forecasters warned that there was still significant uncertainty about its path and potential impacts.


“The knowns are that there’s going to be a strong storm off the New England northeast coast,” said Bob Oravec, a senior meteorologist with the National Weather Service. “The only unknowns are the exact details of the track.”


And that’s a big unknown: if the storm tracks to the west, more rain will fall on the towns and cities between North Carolina and New England. If it tracks to the east, away from land, many of those cities will remain relatively dry. It was far too early on Wednesday for forecasters like Mr. Oravec to say with accuracy what would happen by the weekend, but the picture was beginning to come into focus.


## Here’s what to know


-


**Coastal flooding and erosion** are the most certain threats, as the storm is developing during some of the highest tides of the month.


-


**Rainfall totals** will depend largely on the storm’s precise path, with coastal New England the most likely area to experience what meteorologists call “excessive” rain this weekend.


-


**High winds** will persist across areas at the coast through the end of the week.


-


**More storms may follow:** This is likely the first of several East Coast storms to follow this path over the next few months, driven by[a developing El Niño weather pattern](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/09/weather/el-nino-weather-forecast-facts.html) .


## The Scenarios


“At the moment, our forecast is still emphasizing eastern New England for the heaviest rain,” Mr. Oravec said on Wednesday. “The heaviest rains will definitely be on the coast.”
